status_note: Registered on 2026-11-27 before any QAD-LoRA perplexity was measured. ROADMAP v0.2.3.2 and v0.2.3.3, THME-3105 first slice. The teacher is the unquantized source model; no hosted teacher is used.
student: SmolLM-135M with every weight matrix THME's Q4_0 round-to-nearest recipe touches (q, k, v, o, gate, up, down of every layer, 210 tensors) replaced by its Q4_0 round trip (scripts/train/quant.py, checked bit for bit against THME's own function); embeddings, norms and lm_head unchanged; frozen

method.adapter: LoRA on the seven linear roles, rank 16, alpha 32, no dropout, no bias
method.loss: KL(teacher next-token distribution || student), mean over every position of every window
method.optimizer: AdamW, weight decay 0, constant learning rate, no warm-up, no clipping
method.micro_batch_note: Added before any adapter step or any result existed: the first launch of the pilot ran out of GPU memory with 8 windows per forward pass (49,152-word vocabulary, 16 GB card). The effective batch stays 8 windows: the gradient of 4 pieces of 2 windows equals the gradient of one batch of 8 (tested in scripts/train/test_qad_lora.py). It changes no rule of this protocol.

train.origin: the first 2,490,368 tokens (2,432 windows of 1,024) of the WikiText-2 raw TRAIN split tokenized with the SmolLM-135M tokenizer (scripts/prepare_eval_tokens.py --split train --calibration-windows 0)

validation.origin: the last 65,536 tokens of the same train file; never trained on; used only to pick the learning rate

test.scoring_note: Full test split in consecutive windows of 1024 (thme evaluate defaults), same protocol as the verification reports.

data.disjointness: train and validation come from the WikiText-2 train split and do not overlap each other; the test split is a different split of the corpus (different corpus member, different corpus hash) and is read only by the replication gate (two adapter-free numbers) and the three scored runs

comparators.note: Read from committed reports, not re-run. They were measured on THME's reference path (CPU for RTN and AWQ and GPTQ); this run is measured in PyTorch with THME's windowing, so the replication gate below must pass first.

replication_gate: Before any verdict, the pilot run's own measurements of the unquantized teacher and of the plain Q4_0 student (no adapter) on the TEST file must reproduce THME's committed numbers within 1 percent: ceiling 19.798421901137832 and Q4_0 round-to-nearest 23.698417820506624.

This 1 percent is tighter than the owner's general 5 percent tolerance on purpose: the effects to be detected are 1 to 7 percent, so a 5 percent replication band could not tell a correct replica from a wrong one. The owner may change it before the run.
If the gate fails, no verdict is given and the report states the gap.

pilot.score: perplexity on the validation file after training (lowest wins; ties go to the smaller learning rate)
pilot.note: The test file is read in the pilot only by the replication gate's two adapter-free numbers.

scored_runs.metric: perplexity on the full test split with THME's windowing, student with the adapter (fp32 compute, adapter not merged into Q4_0)

preregistration.noise_scale: sigma = max(sample SD (n-1) of the three scored perplexities, the sample SD of the five AWQ seeds recorded above)
decision_rule: QAD-LoRA beats round-to-nearest only if RTN minus the mean of the three scored perplexities is greater than 2 x sigma.

QAD-LoRA beats AWQ only if the mean AWQ perplexity minus the QAD-LoRA mean is greater than 2 x sigma; it is worse than AWQ only if the QAD-LoRA mean minus the AWQ mean is greater than 2 x sigma; otherwise no difference is shown. The same two tests apply to GPTQ.
Gate: reported for the repository default (v1, at most 0.45 above the ceiling) and for gate v2; the verdict of the gate is read, not judged here.

Drift protocol (docs/research/measurement-drift-protocol.md): the three scored runs are the replicates, the teacher perplexity measured by the first and the last scored run is the reference check against the nominal 19.798421901137832, tolerance 5 percent; a batch outside it is flagged unstable and gives no verdict.

A null or negative result is a valid result and is reported as one. Hyperparameters, seeds, data, the pilot grid, thresholds and this rule are fixed here and are not changed after any scored result is seen; a second configuration would be a new registered run.
preregistration.cost_accounting: adapter bytes, trainable parameters, training seconds and tokens seen (steps x batch x window) are recorded for every run; the recovered model is Q4_0 base plus a floating-point adapter, so it is larger than Q4_0 alone and is not a same-size comparison
preregistration.cross_check: after the scored runs, THME's own thme evaluate is run once on the merged float16 model of seed 1 with an FP16 identity recipe on the same test file; its perplexity should agree with the PyTorch figure of that run within 1 percent (the merged file also carries float16 rounding), which checks the PyTorch evaluation against THME's
limits: one model, one corpus, one configuration; no hyperparameter search beyond the learning-rate pilot
the adapter is not folded back into 4-bit weights, so this measures recovery with an adapter, not a smaller file
training scores every position of a window while evaluation drops the first token of each window (a stated small mismatch)
three seeds measure training noise only; evaluation is deterministic

gate.v2_note: the baseline perplexity is below the switch point 20.0, so v2 uses the same absolute margin

cross_check.what: thme evaluate on the merged float16 model of seed 1 (FP32 identity recipe, same test token file, THME CUDA path) against the PyTorch evaluation of the same run

results.reading: With the pre-registered rule, LoRA recovery on the Q4_0 student beats round-to-nearest (by 3.29), GPTQ (by 1.82) and AWQ (by 1.63) on the SmolLM-135M test split, each far above 2 sigma (0.065); the three seeds agree to 0.018. It recovers most of the quantization loss (round-to-nearest 3.90 above the ceiling, this 0.61 above) but still fails the gate's 0.45 margin. This is a comparison against methods that add no parameters: the recovered model is Q4_0 plus a float32 adapter of 19,593,064 bytes (4,884,480 trainable parameters, about 3.5 percent of the model), so it is larger than Q4_0 alone, and the adapter was not folded back into 4-bit weights.
limits_found: the pilot's best learning rate (1e-3) is the edge of the pre-registered grid, so a higher rate might do better; the grid was not extended after the result, per the protocol
one model, one corpus, one configuration, 256 steps; no claim about other models or longer training
the adapter is evaluated unmerged in float32; the float16 merge adds its own small rounding (checked: THME on the merged file agrees to 0.002 percent)
training scores every position while evaluation drops each window's first token (stated in the protocol)
